newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand ended more than a cent firmer after a spurt of late buying out of London in what was otherwise a dull Monday characterised by low volumes, forex traders said.

The rand's late advance helped bond yields below the 15.90 percent level after hovering around 15.93/94 percent during the day. Bond traders said players took a break after exhaustive trade last week following a one percentage point hike in the official Bank rate.
The rand ended the day at 4.6085/6135 on a buoyant dollar after a 4.6215 high bid in early trade and from 4.6210/6260 at the close on Friday.
"The rand benefited in late trade from buying out of London at the 4.61 level but there was not much action during the day," a senior trader at one of the four "big banks" said.
He said trade was nervous after big fluctuations last week and players were unwilling to hold long dollar positions.
Another senior trader said there was ongoing concern over the tight money market situation which was bound to exert pressure on the currency well into December and mid-January.
"There was some strength today (Monday) but nothing major. Generally, we will probably see the rand trend weaker."
Other traders agreed, anticipating a retracement up to the 4.66/67 level and a peak at 4.72 in the near term.
"I see a test of the topside at 4.66/67 with a peak around 4.72," one predicted.
Traders said they would be monitoring money market liquidity and focusing on the release of October money supply and private sector credit extension figures on Friday which they expected to be poor.
Other local economic data due out this week includes the October trade balance from Wednesday and third quarter GDP figures on Thursday.
The rand managed to extend gains against sterling, firming to 7.7228/7357 from 7.7624/7755 on Friday and was last trading at 0.3289/3294 marks from 0.3248/3253 marks previously.
Bond market yields dipped below 15.90 percent around 1400 GMT on the back of the stronger rand but were trading back above the figure in after-hours trade.
At 1416 GMT the key R150 bond was at 15.89 percent from 15.98 percent previously in thin volume trade.
"It was quiet... possibly in reaction to exhaustive trade last week," one bond trader said.
He said that while last week's interest rate hike had been favourable, the market was still in a bear trend and had not corrected out of sustained selling.
The big event of the week was the release of third quarter GDP figures, trade data and money supply and private credit growth figures -- all due out in the second half of the week.
A second trader put the upside support on the key R150 stock at 15.96 percent with 15.86 percent a big level on the downside.

On the money market, banks quoted their three-month NCD rates unchanged at between 16.95 percent and 17.00 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also steady at between 16.30 and 16.60 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the shortage below nine billion rand at 8.956 billion rand on Saturday from 9.002 billion rand on Friday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners bought a net 41.25 million rand worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 156.55 million rand worth of bonds on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 5.12 billion rand on Friday from 42.57 billion rand on Thursday, a settlement day.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
